subject: Business Models
title: Winner-Take-All Markets
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Winner-Take-All Markets.

hook.text: Google has 92% of global search. Facebook has 77% of social networking. Platforms tend toward monopoly.

buildup.text: Network effects create positive feedback loops: the leading platform attracts more users, widening its lead.

discovery.text: Switching costs compound this. Moving your social graph, photos, or reviews to a competitor is painful.

twist.text: Not all platform markets are winner-take-all. Ride-sharing and food delivery remain fragmented in many regions.

climax.text: Global data effects favor monopoly; local service effects favor competition. The network type decides.

punchline.text: 92% market share. Network effects pick winners decisively.

quiz.question: Why don't all platform markets become monopolies?
options: Local network effects allow regional competition
